reviews.summary: LSK is undergoing a live, material project transition: the Lisk Chain, Portal, Bridge and DAO have just closed. Although exchange-held ERC-20 LSK continues trading, the abrupt utility/governance shift creates elevated event and liquidity/holder-behavior risk.
materialRisks: The Lisk Chain shut down on 2 November 2026; its Portal and Bridge are closed, and assets remaining on the former chain are not guaranteed recoverable pending a planned manual-claims process in January 2027. This is a very recent ecosystem discontinuity.

The Lisk DAO has been wound down and governance infrastructure closed. LSK is now positioned as a loyalty token for a new finance platform, with stated token utility beginning in 2027—creating substantial transition/reclassification risk.
Official supply data shows 49.62M LSK held by Lisk company and 25.86M by Onchain Foundation—about 25.2% of the stated 300M supply—while project-directed buybacks are ongoing through 31 December 2026.

facts.fact: Official status reports no Lisk infrastructure incidents on 4 November 2026; Mainnet, RPC, Sequencer and Batcher are marked operational.
LSK on Ethereum or held at an exchange is described by Lisk as the same token and continues trading; the direct closure risk principally concerns assets left on the former Lisk Chain.
Lisk states total supply is 300M with 0% inflation; 5.24M unassigned/unclaimed staking rewards are slated to be burned after final chain shutdown.
A 26 October–31 December 2026 buyback program has a stated $4.388M budget.
